reuse.why: Keeps using getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate for the moving case, but the new skip rule is not added to that shared weekend helper; getUpcomingDates writes its own skip loop instead of reusing the new findNonWeekend logic.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend => drop weekend occurrences' rule is written three times: findNonWeekend scanning in getNextDate, a separate isWeekend/continue loop in schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates, and isDaily/movesWeekend flags in schedule-template.ts.

placement.why: The core rule sits in shared/schedules.ts, which is right, but callers (schedule-template, getUpcomingDates) each re-derive whether the schedule is daily and whether to move weekends instead of delegating to the shared module.

scope.why: Only the weekend-handling paths, the frequency plumbing in parseRecurDate, a test and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: A future change to the daily/weekend rule has to be found and edited in three files with three different encodings (a flag passed as noSkipWeekend=!isDaily, a movesWeekend ternary, a manual scan loop with an ad-hoc scan cap).

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates decides daily weekend skipping itself with d.isWeekend instead of going through the shared weekend logic in shared/schedules.ts; schedule-template.ts computes movesWeekend locally.

disguised_duplication.where: The weekend-skip scan exists as findNonWeekend in shared/schedules.ts and again reshaped as an inline for-loop with isWeekend/continue and a different scan cap (count*7+14 vs MAX_WEEKEND_SCAN) in schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates.

one_place.where: The rule is decided separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and server/budget/schedule-template.ts (isDaily/movesWeekend); getDateWithSkippedWeekend was not made the single definition.
